**MS-135 resolver record example (2026-11-25).** The resolver record is the shared record from "Resolver inputs and emit shape" above; that section stays the authority for its fields. The MS-135 spellings below carry exactly the same values under the names that fallback, clamp and picker consumers read. A record where an MS-135 spelling and its emit-shape field differ is invalid and is rejected with `resolver_record_invalid`.

| MS-135 field | Same value as | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `requested_model_id` | `requested_model` | string |
| `requested_provider_id?` | `requested_platform` | string, omitted when no provider was requested |
| `account_id?` | `effective_account_id?` | string, omitted when the route has no account |
| `resolved_model_id` | `effective_model` | string |

Fields only MS-135 adds:

| Field | Type | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `capability_snapshot_ref` | string | Ref of the §10.4.3 capability snapshot the resolver read. |
| `credential_route_epoch_id` | string | The MA-067 credential route epoch the effective account used. |
| `fallback_used` | boolean | `true` only when `resolved_model_id` came from a `fallback_chain[]` entry instead of the precedence winner. |
| `clamp_reason?` | string, closed to these members of the `clamp/substitution` reason-code family ("Provider capability and cost gating" above): `effort_unsupported`, `effort_clamped`, `auth_family_capability_clamped`, `capability_unknown`, `instruction_projection_partial`, `skill_projection_partial` | Present only when a requested value was not applied exactly for a reason other than model fallback, with the family's meanings (`effort_clamped` = accepted but narrowed effort; `effort_unsupported` = the effort control is unsupported). The model-level family codes `model_unavailable`, `model_routed_by_provider` and `model_substituted` are never written here: model fallback is `fallback_used = true` with `selection_reason.fallback_reason`. When more than one code applies, the first in this list is recorded and the others stay in the attempt's `EffortSettlementReceipt` and `skipped_persona_controls[]`. Why an effort was narrowed (model maximum, policy ceiling, budget, provider mapping) is the attempt's `EffortSettlementReceipt.clamp_reason`, not this field. |
| `visibility_state` | string, closed: `visible`, `visible_with_notice`, `hidden_from_picker`, `history_only` | Derived from the effective model's `model_lifecycle_state` by the model lifecycle table below. |

**MS-135 model lifecycle transitions (2026-11-25).** `model_lifecycle_state` (§4.1, CV-144) is a catalog-entry state, separate from the provider lifecycle in the acceptance criteria above. A model is dispatchable only when its own state allows it and its provider's state is `healthy` or `degraded`. The allowed transitions are exactly these; every other transition is invalid. A failed or partial catalog refresh never changes `model_lifecycle_state`. Each transition records `from_state`, `to_state`, `trigger`, `evidence_ref` and `transitioned_at_utc`.

| From | To | Trigger |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | `deprecated` | A successful catalog refresh or provider metadata marks the model deprecated; `deprecation_notice_ref?` is recorded. |
| `active` | `sunset_pending` | The provider announces an end date; `sunset_at_utc` and `replacement_model_id?` are recorded. |
| `deprecated` | `sunset_pending` | The provider announces an end date for a deprecated model. |
| `deprecated` | `active` | A later successful catalog refresh no longer marks the model deprecated. |
| `sunset_pending` | `deprecated` | The provider withdraws the end date but keeps the deprecation. |
| `sunset_pending` | `sunset` | `sunset_at_utc` passes. |
| `active`, `deprecated` or `sunset_pending` | `sunset` | The provider stops serving the model before any announced date: a dispatch returns the provider's model-not-found error and the next successful catalog refresh omits the model. |
| `sunset` | `removed` | The provider explicitly lists the model as removed, or two consecutive successful catalog refreshes at least 24 hours apart omit it. |

`removed` is terminal for that catalog entry. If a provider later lists the same model id again, PM creates a new catalog entry generation that starts in `active`; history keeps the removed generation and its receipts.

| `model_lifecycle_state` | New dispatch | `visibility_state` | Model picker shows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | yes | `visible` | the model with no notice |
| `deprecated` | yes | `visible_with_notice` | the model with a "Deprecated" notice and `deprecation_notice_ref?` |
| `sunset_pending` | yes | `visible_with_notice` | the model with an "Ends {sunset_at_utc}" notice and `replacement_model_id?` |
| `sunset` | no, unless an explicit compatibility policy permits it (CV-144) | `hidden_from_picker` | nothing; a run that a compatibility policy lets use it shows "Ended" beside the model name |
| `removed` | no, unless an explicit compatibility policy permits it (CV-144) | `history_only` | nothing; history, receipts and migration lineage still show it |

**MS-135 EffortSettlementReceipt payload (2026-11-25).** One receipt is written for every provider attempt, and a fresh one for every model switch, compaction, resume or subagent spawn. Effort values are the provider/model-specific labels from the capability snapshot (for example `high`, `max` or `thinking`), never a generic ladder (MS-115).

| Field | Type | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `receipt_id` | string | Unique per receipt. |
| `attempt_id` | string | The provider attempt this settles. |
| `model_id` | string | Effective model of the attempt. |
| `account_id` | string or null | Effective account; null when the route has no account. |
| `capability_snapshot_ref` | string | Snapshot whose effort support was read. |
| `requested_effort` | string or null | The label requested for this run; null when none was requested. |
| `policy_effort` | string or null | The label after scope policy ceilings; null when no policy applied. |
| `effective_effort` | string or null | The label actually honored; null when the route has no effort control or the request was skipped. |
| `effective_wire_effort` | string or null | The exact provider-native value sent, such as `high` for `model_reasoning_effort`. |
| `provider_native_field` | string or null | The provider field it was sent in, such as `model_reasoning_effort` or `thinking`. |
| `display_label` | string | The label the GUI shows for the effective effort: the effort label, optionally followed by one space and one parenthesized notice such as `(Max not supported)`. |

### Terminal Fixture Matrix And Record Minima

Repairs rows `sfk-c5ad7b33fa51846ef1c86c49` and `sfk-e9cc3bc253470d324d189932`.

Terminal VT/xterm/OSC fixtures are grouped by `fixture_id`, `protocol_family`, `input_bytes_ref`, `expected_screen_hash`, `expected_event_refs[]`, and `negative_case`. The fixture rows themselves, with their replay byte streams and expected results, are `### Terminal protocol fixture rows` in the 2026-11-25 addendum at the end of this document.

Required record minima:

- `TerminalIngestionReceipt`: `receipt_id`, `terminal_session_id`, `stage`, `byte_count`, `protocol_family`, `accepted`, `rejected_reason_code?`, `transcript_chunk_refs[]?`, `created_at_utc`.
- `TerminalBackpressureState`: `terminal_session_id`, `queue_depth`, `dropped_frame_count`, `throttle_state`, `last_transition_at_utc`.
- `TerminalRenderFrame`: `frame_id`, `terminal_session_id`, `dirty_region_refs[]`, `screen_hash`, `rendered_at_utc`.
- `TerminalInputEvent`: `event_id`, `terminal_session_id`, `input_kind`, `payload_ref`, `permission_snapshot_id?`, `created_at_utc`.
- `TerminalPasteReceipt`: `receipt_id`, `terminal_session_id`, `paste_kind`, `byte_count`, `sanitized`, `created_at_utc`.
- `TerminalOscEvent`: `event_id`, `terminal_session_id`, `osc_code`, `payload_ref`, `allowed`, `blocked_reason_code?`.
- `TerminalScrollbackAnchor`: `anchor_id`, `terminal_session_id`, `line_offset`, `screen_hash`, `created_at_utc`.
- `TerminalProfileResolution`: `resolution_id`, `profile_id`, `shell_path`, `cwd`, `env_summary_ref`, `created_at_utc`.
- `TerminalSessionRestoreDecision`: `decision_id`, `terminal_session_id`, `restore_state`, `reason_code`, `created_at_utc`.
- `TerminalAccessibilitySnapshot`: `snapshot_id`, `terminal_session_id`, `screen_reader_text_ref`, `focus_cell`, `created_at_utc`.
- `TerminalDiagnosticsEnvelope`: `diagnostic_id`, `terminal_session_id`, `category`, `severity`, `message_ref`, `created_at_utc`.

`TerminalScrollbackAnchor` is a record minimum, not proof of retained content or complete output. Its resolution must satisfy the Terminal output read semantics above, including source identity, whole-range backing validity, mutation handling, and logical-text preservation across ordinary reflow. Each of these eleven records has the closed wire shape, field types and owner given in `### Terminal record wire contract` in the 2026-11-25 addendum at the end of this document.

### Terminal record wire contract

The eleven records of `### Terminal Fixture Matrix And Record Minima` are values of the Puppet Master terminal engine (`#SMPFS-184`). Their owner is the engine instance of the one terminal session named by `terminal_session_id` (`TerminalProfileResolution`: the engine instance that is starting that session); they live in memory for that session and are dropped when it ends. None of them is a storage family, a storage value, an EventRecord or a seglog row. What a terminal keeps across restarts is exactly what `Plans/storage-plan.md#SP-332` keeps (the session record and the saved scrollback with its command records); none of these eleven is added to it, and a restored tab mints new anchors rather than reading old ones.

**Export policy.** The user-requested diagnostic bundle of `#SMPFS-076` is the one export these records have. When the user asks for a bundle, the engine writes into it a copy of the session's records whose row below names the diagnostic bundle, each serialized by the wire shape below and within its row's content limits: the content behind a `payload_ref`, `env_summary_ref` or `message_ref` stays out unless `#SMPFS-076` labels it as included transcript content, and shell content enters the bundle only as transcript content it labels absent, partial or included. `TerminalRenderFrame`, `TerminalScrollbackAnchor` and `TerminalAccessibilitySnapshot` name no bundle and are never in one. The bundle is a file the user asked for at one moment, not a storage family, backup or sync: the in-memory records it copied are still dropped when the session ends, and Puppet Master never reads a bundle back to restore a session or a record. Writing the bundle passes FileSafe's redaction (`Plans/FileSafe.md#F2-195`) and trace persistence steps (`Plans/FileSafe.md#section=Trace persistence limits and sampling rule (2026-11-25)`, quota class `support_bundle`); a bundle for a session outside any run has FileSafe's runless quota owner `diagnostic_bundle`. When the bundle includes transcript bytes, the session's `TerminalIngestionReceipt` with `stage` `diagnostic_exported` records them by the table's per-read rule; that receipt is an in-memory record like the others. No other export, sync or backup ever carries one of these records.

**Wire shape.** When a record leaves the engine it is one JSON object (RFC 8259, UTF-8) with exactly the record's minimum fields plus `record_type`, a constant equal to the record name, and `schema_version`, the constant `"1.0.0"`. Unknown fields, missing required fields and values outside the types below are refused; a field marked `?` may be absent but is never `null`. A record leaves the engine only over the boundaries its row names: the web GUI terminal transport (DL-139, `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md#F3-583`), the user-requested diagnostic bundle (`#SMPFS-076`, which carries shell content only as transcript content it labels absent, partial or included), the in-process accessibility bridge (`#SMPFS-126`, `#SMPFS-131`), and agent reads (`#SMPFS-182`).

**Field types.** `id`: string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$`. `utc`: RFC 3339 instant ending in `Z`. `count`: integer 0 to 2^64−1. `ref`: opaque string of 1 to 256 bytes naming an in-memory buffer of the same session; it is never a path and never carries the content. Inside the engine's process (the accessibility bridge and agent reads) the reader resolves a `ref` against the engine's own buffer. The web GUI terminal transport crosses a process boundary, and the remote web client shares no memory with the Server's engine, so there a `ref` is resolved against the transport message rather than shared memory: the message that carries a record also carries, beside the record object and keyed by the record's `ref` value, the content the receiving side needs, and the receiver keeps that content under the same `ref` in its own copy of the session for as long as the session's buffer would.   - Locked function contract (2026-11-25; the `-> String` signature in ARC-009 stays as an illustration of the formatted text only): the pipeline is `get_agent_rules_context(request: &AgentRulesContextRequest) -> AgentRulesContextResult`. It never panics and never returns a bare string; every outcome is a result. Each `warnings[]` and `errors[]` entry is `{code, source_path?, detail}` where `code` is closed. Warning codes: `project_rules_missing` (a project is set but `.puppet-master/project-rules.md` does not exist; Project rules are omitted), `scoped_agents_skipped` (a scoped `AGENTS.md` was outside the cone or disabled by `scoped_agents_enabled`), `budget_threshold_exceeded` (bytes over the warn threshold, non-strict), `truncated` (deterministic truncation per ARC-029 removed illustrative sections; ARC-030 records it). No caller may fall back to a partial block, for example application rules alone when project rules exist but are unreadable. The pipeline does not retry. A read error is evaluated again only when the caller starts again or the user retries; `invalid_request` and `budget_exceeded_strict` stay failed until their input changes.
  - Typed request (2026-11-26; carries ARC-009's scope-aware input, so the field list in the bullet above is extended, not replaced). `AgentRulesContextRequest`: `request_id` string (UUID); `caller` closed enum `orchestrator | interview | assistant`; `computer_id` string (required: the actual work Computer whose applicable application context is read, ARC-004; it is never a Project identity); `thread_id?` string and `run_id?` string (the application/thread identity: Interview and Assistant carry `thread_id`; Orchestrator carries `run_id`, plus the `thread_id` of the thread that started the run when there is one; at least one of the two is present); `project_id?` string and `project_rules_ref?` string (present together exactly when a Project is bound; both absent is `project_path=None`, which omits Project rules only); `application_rules_ref` string; `source_revisions[]` array of `{source_ref, revision}` objects, both strings, with one entry for each source the caller resolved: the application-rules record `app.agent_rules.application_markdown` (always), the work Computer's application context (when it exists) and `.puppet-master/project-rules.md` (always when a Project is bound: its revision is the SHA-256 of the file bytes when the file exists, and the literal string `absent` when it does not); `scoped_agents_enabled` boolean; `max_bytes` integer, at least 1; `created_at_utc` string (RFC 3339 UTC).
